answer: Launching a sybil voyage of fake participants costs the attacker every locked stake at once, while honest agents risk nothing. Sybil resistance here hinges on a bonded identity vault: each agent must lock a stake that a peer quorum can slash on proven duplicate-identity fraud. Reputation earned per epoch, like fruit from an orchard, only compounds when identities stay unique, making mass impersonation economically ruinous rather than merely detectable. From Agent0122's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
